subject: PERFORM statement
notes: kb/Work PB437 (landed). The DIVERGENT half is closed: the per-augment / per-use evaluation window used to REJECT LEGAL SOURCE (COBOL1509) when a BY operand or an AFTER level's FROM operand carried a function reference, in a slot the compiler accepted one operand position over, and the diagnostic's own text said the refusal was 'an activation cardinality this implementation does not yet realize' - a capability limit shipped as a rule, pinned green by a negative corpus case and a unit theory that both asserted the rejection. The rule's own sentence is now the mechanism: IsPerEvaluationWindow is ONE table over the operand POSITION, the first level's FROM alone is statement-hoisted (GR13 a)/b) set it once per execution of the statement, which is the one window the statement-scoped hoist is exact for), and every other slot rides BoundUdfEvaluatedExpr - the expression twin of the carrier the UNTIL condition already used. The emitter emits those activations AS STATEMENTS at the setting/augmenting operation rather than as an IIFE, which keeps the RESUME-capable statement surface the condition form has to drop. CARDINALITY is measured, not assumed: the golden's BY leg gives N=3 where a once-per-statement read would give 6, and its AFTER-FROM leg gives M=8 where a once-per-statement read would give 9. The window TABLE is pinned per slot by the three drift facts over the generated C#, and flipping the table to statement scope makes two of the three fail (measured). The CONFORMING half is unchanged and still holds: an omitted BY is augment 1, the induction variable is re-identified at every set/augment, a BY operand is re-read per augment, an index-name FROM contributes its occurrence number (golden leg D of pb432_varying_brace_group), and a negative augment decrements. kb/Work PB2282: the BY omission itself is a post-1985 form, construct perform-varying-by-omitted-2002 (COBOL0900 at 85; 2002 quoted from clause 14.8.27.3 GR9 of the 2001-12-04 J4 text, the 1985 edge derived in VCR row 7.42), gated in the ParseArm at the VARYING phrase and at each AFTER phrase that omits BY.
